parameters.query:
-- Close any agent_runs row the failed execution left at 'running'.
-- Workflows record $execution.id in agent_runs.input, which is the only link
-- between an n8n execution and its audit row.
--
-- Zero matched rows is a normal outcome: the workflow may have failed before it
-- opened a run, or it may not call a model at all. The CTE is wrapped in an
-- aggregate so this query always returns exactly one summary row, whether or not
-- anything was closed.
--
-- COALESCE guards agent_runs_error_requires_message. Only 'running' rows are
-- touched, so a run that already reached a terminal status is never overwritten.
WITH closed AS (
    UPDATE agent_runs
    SET status      = 'error',
        error       = COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'Workflow failed with no error message'),
        finished_at = now()
    WHERE status = 'running'
      AND input ->> 'execution_id' = ($1::jsonb ->> 'execution_id')
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT count(*)::int                      AS runs_closed,
       COALESCE(json_agg(id), '[]'::json) AS closed_run_ids,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'execution_id'       AS execution_id,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'workflow_name'      AS workflow_name
FROM closed;

nodes.name: Close Agent Runs
nodes.notes: A row left at 'running' is how WF-101 spots a workflow that died. This closes it.

parameters.query:
-- Queue the failure for delivery, deduplicated.
--
-- docs/workflows.md requires this on WF-99: "deduplicated so one broken
-- schedule does not send 96 messages a day". The rule itself lives in
-- queue_notification (0011_notifications.sql) so that every workflow gets the
-- same behaviour and none of them can opt out of it by mistake.
--
-- This node must not be able to fail the error handler. It writes one row with
-- no joins and no casts that can throw; WF-99 has no error workflow of its own
-- on purpose, so a failure here would be silent.
SELECT q.notification_id,
       q.status,
       q.occurrences,
       q.deduplicated,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'dedup_key' AS dedup_key
FROM queue_notification(
         'agent_failure',
         $1::jsonb ->> 'dedup_key',
         $1::jsonb ->> 'title',
         $1::jsonb ->> 'body',
         'immediate',
         $1::jsonb -> 'payload',
         NULL,
         NULL,
         make_interval(mins => ($1::jsonb ->> 'cooloff_minutes')::int)
     ) q;
